clay.definition: A soft material shaped by hand to make objects.

slip.definition: Potter's clay that is thinned and used for coating or decorating ceramics.

glaze.definition: A glassy coating put on clay and hardened by heat.

underglaze.definition: A colored ceramic decoration applied before a transparent or other glaze is added and fired.
underglaze.exampleUsage: The artist painted the design with underglaze.

engobe.definition: A clay slip which is colored with metal oxides or stains, used for coating the surface of a pot either before or after bisque firing.

oxide.definition: Any compound of oxygen with another element or a radical.

stain.definition: To color with a liquid dye or tint.

grog.definition: Ground fired clay mixed into fresh clay to strengthen it.

porcelain.definition: Ceramic ware made of a more or less translucent ceramic.

stoneware.definition: Ceramic ware that is fired in high heat and vitrified and nonporous.

potter-s-wheel.definition: A rotating platform used by potters to shape clay into round forms.
potter-s-wheel.exampleUsage: The potter centered the clay on the potter's wheel.

wire-cutter.definition: A hand tool with two sharp edges designed to cut wire.
wire-cutter.exampleUsage: The wire cutter was used during the activity.

needle-tool.definition: A sharp pointed pottery tool used by trained users for cutting, scoring, measuring, or trimming clay.
needle-tool.exampleUsage: The needle tool was stored safely after the demonstration.

rib.definition: Support resembling the rib of an animal.
rib.exampleUsage: The rib was identified during the lesson.

loop-tool.definition: A pottery tool with a loop of metal used to trim, carve, or remove clay.
loop-tool.exampleUsage: The potter used a loop tool to refine the surface.

trimming-tool.definition: A pottery tool used to remove excess clay and refine the shape of a partly dried piece.
trimming-tool.exampleUsage: The trimming tool refined the base of the bowl.

carving-tool.definition: A tool used to cut decorative lines, textures, or shapes into clay.
carving-tool.exampleUsage: The artist used a carving tool to add a simple pattern.

stamp.definition: A carved or raised object used to print the same design repeatedly.

throwing.definition: Sending an object through the air with your hand.

coiling.definition: A pottery method that builds a form from long rolls of clay.

slab-building.definition: A pottery method that forms objects from flat sheets of clay joined together.
slab-building.exampleUsage: The class used slab building to make a small box.

pinching.definition: A pottery-forming technique that shapes soft clay by pressing and pinching it with the fingers.
pinching.exampleUsage: Pinching was used to shape a small bowl.

glazing.definition: The process of applying a glass-forming ceramic coating that becomes fused to pottery during firing.
glazing.exampleUsage: Glazing gave the fired piece a glossy surface.

scoring.definition: Evaluation of performance by assigning a grade or score.

wedging.definition: A pottery preparation process that kneads clay to make its consistency more even and reduce trapped air.
wedging.exampleUsage: The teacher demonstrated wedging before students began shaping clay.

centering.definition: The concentration of attention or energy on something.

pulling.definition: Shaping a clay wall upward with the hands on a pottery wheel.

kiln.definition: A special oven used to fire clay and make it hard.

kiln-shelf.definition: A heat-resistant flat shelf that supports ceramic pieces inside a kiln during firing.
kiln-shelf.exampleUsage: The pottery pieces were spaced on the kiln shelf.

kiln-post.definition: A heat-resistant support used to hold kiln shelves at different heights.
kiln-post.exampleUsage: Kiln posts supported the shelf inside the kiln.

thermocouple.definition: A kind of thermometer consisting of two wires of different metals that are joined at both ends.

pyrometric-cone.definition: A temperature-measuring device made from several cones, each designed to melt at a different temperature.
pyrometric-cone.exampleUsage: The pyrometric cone was used during the activity.

firing-log.definition: A written record of kiln firings, including information such as date, program, temperature, and results.
firing-log.exampleUsage: The instructor recorded the firing in the firing log.

glaze-bucket.definition: A container used to hold liquid ceramic glaze in a pottery studio.
glaze-bucket.exampleUsage: The glaze bucket was labeled with the glaze name.

kiln-wash.definition: A refractory coating applied to kiln shelves to help keep melted glaze from sticking permanently to them.
kiln-wash.exampleUsage: The studio maintains kiln shelves with kiln wash.

ventilation-fan.definition: A fan used to move air and remove heat, fumes, or airborne particles from an indoor work area.
ventilation-fan.exampleUsage: The ventilation fan helps move air out of the studio.

heat-resistant-gloves.definition: Protective gloves designed to reduce heat transfer to the hands when handling hot objects.
heat-resistant-gloves.exampleUsage: Heat-resistant gloves are part of the studio's protective equipment.

teapot.definition: A container with a spout and handle used to brew and pour tea.

tile.definition: A flat thin rectangular slab (as of fired clay or rubber or linoleum) used to cover surfaces.

sculpture.definition: A three-dimensional work of plastic art.

planter.definition: The owner or manager of a plantation.

candle-holder.definition: A holder that keeps a candle upright while it burns.

work-table.definition: A table built to support a specific kind of work.

wedging-table.definition: A sturdy worktable with a suitable surface for preparing and kneading clay.
wedging-table.exampleUsage: The potter prepared clay on the wedging table.

sink.definition: A bowl with taps and a drain, used for washing your hands or face.

splash-pan.definition: A tray or pan around a potter's wheel that catches water and clay thrown outward while the wheel turns.
splash-pan.exampleUsage: The splash pan kept wet clay from reaching the floor.
splash-pan.arabicTranslation: حوض مانع للرذاذ حول عجلة الفخار

drying-rack.definition: A shelf unit used to hold pottery while it dries before later stages of finishing or firing.
drying-rack.exampleUsage: The unfinished bowls were placed on the drying rack.

storage-shelf.definition: A shelf used to keep materials, tools, or finished items organized.
storage-shelf.exampleUsage: Clay tools were arranged on the storage shelf.

bucket.definition: The quantity contained in a bucket.

bat.definition: A wooden stick used to hit a ball.

turntable.definition: A revolving tray placed on a dining table.

wheel.definition: Game equipment consisting of a wheel with slots that is used for gambling.

sculpting-tool.definition: A tool used to shape or smooth clay.
sculpting-tool.exampleUsage: The sculpting tool was used during the activity.

needle.definition: A thin pointed tool used for sewing or shaping clay.

wax.definition: A coating applied to pottery to prevent glaze from sticking.

figurine.definition: A small carved or molded figure.
